title: 以为钱到位就行：旧系统还得接着跑，新系统怎么塞进去
speaker: George Ferguson

segments.en: over national airport, a lot of impulse to get this taken care of more quickly. I mean, they've been talked for years, of course, in modernizing the system, but I thought that we were
segments.zh: 在全国机场，有很多推动力要更快解决这个问题。我的意思是，他们多年来一直在讨论系统现代化，但我以为我们

segments.en: well on the way to that happening. What's your sense of the status of this? And as we hear the Transportation Secretary talk about the need for $50 billion to do all of this,
segments.zh: 已经进展顺利。你怎么看目前的状况？当我们听到交通部长谈到需要500亿美元来完成所有这些，

segments.en: what accounts for the hold up? Again, I think you've got to build it into a system that's working today and you can't shut the system down to rejuvenate the whole thing, right? So the challenge is
segments.zh: 阻碍是什么？再次，我认为你必须把它融入今天正在运行的系统，你不能为了更新整个系统而关闭它，对吧？所以挑战是

segments.en: how do you build new better systems into old existing systems and don't hurt safety?
segments.zh: 如何将新的更好的系统融入旧的现有系统，同时不损害安全？

segments.en: I think they're constantly making improvements to the network, but technologies come a long way and air travel continues to grow three, four percent a year and so the burdens continue to rise
segments.zh: 我认为他们在不断改进网络，但技术已经走了很长一段路，航空旅行继续以每年3%、4%的速度增长，所以负担继续上升

segments.en: in the system. So my sense is we're behind the curve and I think we probably need to spend more money but more effort to get ahead of the curve, right? A lot of times what I find nowadays is not
segments.zh: 在系统中。所以我的感觉是我们落后了，我认为我们可能需要花更多的钱，但更多的努力来领先，对吧？很多时候我现在发现不是
